summary: Intermittent cross-region handoffs from EU pin causing p95 latency spikes; DNS/subnet affinity suspected
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes for EU-region requests even when the request is pinned to eu-west. Spikes correlate with a subset of requests showing cross-region handoff to apac-southeast. Customer enabled region pinning/residency and expects traffic to remain in eu-west.

Impact:
- BrightCart is seeing p95 spikes from ~180ms baseline to 1.6–2s for ~5-10% of EU requests during their morning traffic window.
- Affects order validation and search autocomplete features (user-facing).

Environment:
- Customer on Enterprise plan with dedicated tenancy for EU (BrightCart production).
- Requests originate from BrightCart EU devices and pass through their VPC peering.
- Redwood API requests show X-Region-Pin header set to eu-west.

Expected behavior:
- With region pinning enabled, requests should remain served from eu-west or fall back deterministically to a configured variant without cross-region hops.

Observed behavior:
- ~5-10% of requests show route path eu-west -> apac-southeast with increased RTT.
- Happens in bursts lasting 30s–2m, often aligned with internal CDN/edge rebalance events.

Additional notes:
- Customer runs some client-side DNS resolvers in their VPC (custom DNS/forwarders).
- They have strict residency toggles enabled in the Console for EU traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightCart EU API key and set header X-Region-Pin: eu-west
2) Send a steady stream of lightweight generation requests (50rps) to /v1/generate for model redwood-open-compat-7b
3) Observe p50/p95 and inspect X-Request-Path and X-Serving-Node headers in responses
4) Reproduce during EU morning window where customer reports spikes (09:00-11:00 CET)
5) Optionally toggle residency strict mode in Console and repeat to compare behavior
logs: 2026-03-09T09:17:32Z request_id=rc-8f3a path=/v1/generate X-Region-Pin=eu-west served_from=apac-southeast latency=1698ms edge_node=eu-edge-17 note=handed-off
2026-03-09T09:17:33Z request_id=rc-8f3b path=/v1/generate X-Region-Pin=eu-west served_from=eu-west latency=182ms edge_node=eu-edge-12
2026-03-09T09:18:01Z router-event edge-rebalance start eu-edge-17 -> draining; affected_sessions=0.08
Client-side resolver logs (provided by customer) show DNS TTL refreshes at 30s intervals coincident with spike windows
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support on 2026-03-10: pattern of bursts tied to edge rebalancing events. SRE checked routing tables and found that during edge node drain events the router emits a handoff to available capacity; handoff logic respects pin only if upstream edge advertises 'pin-affinity' tag.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- Customer's VPC-level DNS resolver refreshes cached next-hop records on a 30s cadence which, combined with short-lived edge rebalances, allows some requests to land on an edge that does not currently advertise pin-affinity, causing cross-region handoff to apac-southeast.
- Our edge-level DNS cache currently has a short negative cache TTL which can allow transient resolution to a remote POP when local POP connectivity briefly degrades.

Metrics checked:
- Router handoff rate spiked at 09:17 CET matching customer p95 spikes.
- Edge drain events logged from internal autoscaler at same timestamps.

Temporary workaround applied 2026-03-12 by Support:
- Recommended BrightCart enable 'strict residency' toggle for the affected API key (Console) and increase client DNS resolver TTL caching to >120s to avoid mid-session next-hop flips.
- Support flagged routing rule change to prefer local POPs when X-Region-Pin header present (config gate closed to rollout).

2026-03-10 13:21 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Checked router metrics. Found edge rebalancing events at 09:17 CET causing short-lived handoffs. Suspect DNS/refresher interplay. Adding INT ticket for infra investigation (INT-981).
2026-03-11 08:45 - BrightCart Support (BrightCart SRE): Provided VPC DNS forwarder logs showing TTL rotations every 30s. Confirmed spikes drop when they manually increase resolver cache to 180s.
2026-03-12 09:12 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Deployed a canary change to prefer local POP when X-Region-Pin present on staging. Metrics look promising on staging with p95 improvements.

2026-03-13 16:05 - Product Ops (Lena Cho): Noted product implications; requested a config toggle for dedicated customers to default to strict residency on new keys until router fix is fully rolled out.

2026-03-14 09:30 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Rolling plan: 1) Harden router to require pin-affinity on handoff paths (canary) 2) Adjust negative DNS cache behavior on edges 3) Documentation update and support playbook to advise customers on DNS TTL best-practices. Assigned follow-up tasks to infra team.
resolution: Ongoing. Workaround provided to customer: enable strict residency toggle and increase client DNS resolver cache to >=120s. Canary routing change validated on staging; production rollout planned with phased canary and monitoring. Infra team to land DNS negative-cache adjustment (PR infra/dns#127). Support to follow up with customer after rollout and verify p95 stabilizes for two business windows.
